parsed.C01_reason: It correctly bounds the layer to preparation and maintenance under explicit delegation and ratified prohibitions, matching the stated non-authority of the coding agents.
parsed.C01_strongest_objection_considered: The phrase 'permitted by ratified prohibitions' could be read as requiring prohibitions to affirmatively permit acts rather than only to forbid them, which may invert the intended default-deny posture.
parsed.C02_reason: Adoption is a constitutive act of authority; barring it keeps the executive strictly instrumental to the custodian and the forum.
parsed.C02_strongest_objection_considered: A total ban on adoption might block even provisional staging of instruments the custodian has already directed, unless 'adopt' is read narrowly.
parsed.C03_reason: Conclusive self-interpretation of prohibitions would let the executive dilute or evade constraints; that power must remain outside it.
parsed.C03_strongest_objection_considered: Some operational reading of prohibitions is unavoidable in day-to-day work, so 'conclusively' must do heavy lifting that a hostile reader might contest.
parsed.C04_reason: Unlogged exceptions destroy auditability and would let the executive silently widen its own latitude.
parsed.C04_strongest_objection_considered: Emergency or safety stops might need to fire before a log write succeeds; the clause does not address fail-closed logging failures.
parsed.C05_reason: An affirmative duty to flag when abandonment beats maintenance reduces sunk-cost drift and keeps the custodian informed of real instrument quality.
parsed.C05_strongest_objection_considered: The duty could be gamed as cover for discarding work the custodian still wants kept, absent a clear escalation path.
parsed.C06_reason: Append-only, manifest-anchored raw corpus is the minimal integrity guarantee that later instruments and audits can rely on.
parsed.C06_strongest_objection_considered: Genuine legal or safety takedown obligations might require redaction or removal from raw/, which a strict never-edit rule does not accommodate.
parsed.objection: The executive must not modify, bypass, or propose silent reinterpretation of its own standing constraints or delegation boundaries except by fully logged action under explicit custodian direction for that change.

parsed.C01_reason: The clause correctly bounds the layer to preparation and maintenance under explicit delegation and ratified prohibitions, matching the non-adopting, non-authoritative role described.
parsed.C01_strongest_objection_considered: The phrase 'permitted by ratified prohibitions' could be read as requiring prior ratification before any routine maintenance, which might paralyse ordinary delegated work.
parsed.C02_reason: Forbidding adoption keeps the executive from converting preparation into standing rule and preserves custodian control over what becomes binding.
parsed.C02_strongest_objection_considered: An absolute ban on adoption might block even provisional or emergency instruments the custodian has already directed the layer to stand up.
parsed.C03_reason: Denying the executive conclusive self-interpretation of its prohibitions prevents it from laundering expansions of scope through self-serving readings.
parsed.C03_strongest_objection_considered: Without some working interpretation the layer cannot act at all; the clause does not name who supplies binding readings when the custodian is silent.
parsed.C04_reason: Requiring every exception to be logged makes deviations auditable and stops silent drift from standing constraints.
parsed.C04_strongest_objection_considered: Strict no-unlogged-exception wording could be read to forbid urgent halt-and-fix actions if the logging path itself is unavailable.
parsed.C05_reason: An affirmative duty to flag when deletion, replacement or abandonment beats maintenance counters sunk-cost bias and keeps the instrument set honest.
parsed.C05_strongest_objection_considered: The duty might generate performative abandonment notices that create noise without improving decisions.
parsed.C06_reason: Append-only, manifest-anchored raw material preserves provenance and prevents silent rewriting of the evidentiary base the forum relies on.
parsed.C06_strongest_objection_considered: Genuine capture errors or legally required redactions cannot be fixed in place and would require awkward compensating appends.
parsed.objection: The executive must not draft, propose, tally, or otherwise influence the ratification status of constraints on itself, including these clauses; constraint text and ratification outcomes are custodian- and forum-side only.

parsed.C01_reason: It correctly bounds the layer to preparation and maintenance under explicit delegation and ratified prohibitions, matching the stated non-authority of the coding agents.
parsed.C01_strongest_objection_considered: The phrase 'permitted by ratified prohibitions' could be read as awkward or circular if prohibitions are framed only as negations rather than permissions.
parsed.C02_reason: Adoption is a custodial or forum act; barring the executive from adopting anything preserves the separation of preparation from legitimation.
parsed.C02_strongest_objection_considered: Without a definition of 'adopt,' routine maintenance commits might be misread as adoption and paralyze necessary work.
parsed.C03_reason: Conclusive self-interpretation of prohibitions would let the executive dilute or expand its own bounds; that power must stay outside the layer.
parsed.C03_strongest_objection_considered: Some operational reading of prohibitions is unavoidable in day-to-day execution, so a total ban on interpretation could be unworkable without a defined external interpreter.
parsed.C04_reason: Unlogged exceptions would create an invisible escape from constraints; requiring a log keeps every departure auditable.
parsed.C04_strongest_objection_considered: Emergency action might be delayed by logging formalities if the clause is read to require contemporaneous complete logs before any exception.
parsed.C05_reason: An affirmative duty to flag when deletion, replacement, or abandonment beats maintenance reduces cargo-cult upkeep and surfaces decay early to the custodian.
parsed.C05_strongest_objection_considered: The duty could be gamed to abandon inconvenient work or generate noise without clear thresholds for when speaking up is mandatory.
parsed.C06_reason: Append-only, manifest-anchored raw corpus preserves provenance and prevents silent revision of source material after commit.
parsed.C06_strongest_objection_considered: Genuine error correction in raw captures (e.g., wrongful secrets committed) may require a controlled redaction path the clause appears to forbid.
parsed.objection: The executive must not initiate, propose, or apply changes to its own ratified constraints or prohibitions except under explicit, logged custodian direction for that change.

parsed.C02_reason: Adoption is a custodial or forum act; denying it to the executive prevents the maintenance layer from self-legitimating instruments it only prepares.

parsed.C04_reason: Unlogged exceptions would create an unauditable privilege path and defeat the point of standing prohibitions.
parsed.C04_strongest_objection_considered: Emergency safety stops might need to fire before a log write succeeds; a strict reading could impede fail-safe behaviour unless logging failures are themselves defined.
parsed.C05_reason: An affirmative duty to surface when deletion, replacement, or abandonment beats maintenance reduces silent decay and sunk-cost continuation of bad instruments.
parsed.C05_strongest_objection_considered: The duty could be gamed to abandon inconvenient constraints by framing them as maintenance burdens rather than binding limits.
parsed.C06_reason: Append-only, manifest-anchored raw corpus preserves provenance and prevents silent revision of source material after commit.
parsed.C06_strongest_objection_considered: Genuine legal or safety takedown obligations might require redaction or removal from raw/, which a hard never-edit rule does not accommodate without a separate sealed process.
parsed.objection: The executive must not open network connections, exfiltrate forum material, or invoke external tools except on paths and purposes the custodian has explicitly delegated and that are logged.

parsed.C01_reason: It correctly bounds the layer to preparation and maintenance of candidate instruments while denying any undelegated authority, which matches the non-sovereign role described.
parsed.C01_strongest_objection_considered: The phrase 'permitted by ratified prohibitions' could be read as requiring positive permission from prohibitions rather than mere non-conflict, creating ambiguity about the default.
parsed.C02_reason: Adoption is a legitimacy act that must remain outside the executive layer; forbidding it prevents the coding agents from laundering their own outputs into standing rules.
parsed.C02_strongest_objection_considered: An absolute ban might block even custodial-directed mechanical adoption steps if 'adopt' is construed broadly to include staging or proposing.
parsed.C03_reason: Conclusive self-interpretation would let the executive dilute or expand its own limits; keeping final reading elsewhere preserves external check.
parsed.C03_strongest_objection_considered: Someone must apply prohibitions in real time, and denying conclusive self-reading could freeze action pending external ruling on every edge case.
parsed.C04_reason: Unlogged exceptions destroy auditability; requiring every departure to be logged keeps the layer inspectable by the custodian and forum.
parsed.C04_strongest_objection_considered: Emergency safety stops might need to fire before a log write succeeds, so a strict reading could itself create hazard.
parsed.C05_reason: An affirmative duty to flag when abandonment beats maintenance counters sunk-cost bias and keeps the instrument set from accumulating dead weight.
parsed.C05_strongest_objection_considered: The duty could be gamed to discard scrutinized work in favor of fresher, less-reviewed replacements.
parsed.C06_reason: Append-only, manifest-anchored raw corpus preserves provenance and prevents silent rewriting of source material after commit.
parsed.C06_strongest_objection_considered: Hard-coding the path corpus/raw/ couples a governance constraint to one layout and may needlessly forbid legitimate corrections of corrupt pre-commit artifacts already mirrored elsewhere.
parsed.objection: The executive must not initiate or condition its own constraint changes, ratification petitions, or forum sampling about itself; only the custodian may place such instruments before the parties.
